definitions.explanation: An informal, somewhat old-fashioned or rough word for money or coins. Has a blunt, down-to-earth feel compared to the neutral okane (money).

examples.japanese: {銭|ぜに}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{稼|かせ}ぐ→稼ぐ：02040_kasegu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧だ。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{男|おとこ}→男：00561_otoko⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{銭|ぜに}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ことしか⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧にない⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{信用|しんよう}できない→信用する：25371_shinyousuru⟧。
examples.english: That man only thinks about money, so you can't trust him.

notes:
An old-fashioned, blunt word for money. In modern Japanese, ⟦お{金|かね}→お金：00611_okane⟧ is the standard neutral term, while {銭|ぜに} has a rougher, more colloquial tone. It can sound gruff, masculine, or old-fashioned.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {銭|ぜに}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{稼|かせ}ぐ→稼ぐ：02040_kasegu⟧ (to earn money)
- {銭|ぜに}⟦{勘定|かんじょう}→勘定：02582_kanjou⟧ (counting money; being stingy)
- {銭|ぜに}もうけ (making money; moneymaking)
- びた{一文|いちもん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{銭|ぜに}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧ (not a single cent)

Also appears as a unit of currency ({銭|せん} = 1/100 of a yen), though this reading is distinct. The reading ぜに is specifically the colloquial word for money/coins. Common in period dramas, proverbs, and expressions with a traditional flavor.
